# neatHack Build Log: FirstRun

## Project

- **Name:** FirstRun
- **Purpose:** FirstRun runs your quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, and proves the fix with a second clean run.
- **Problem:** Quickstarts break when a package is renamed, a flag is removed or a version moves. Nobody on the team gets an alert. The first person who finds the break is a new user, and most new users leave.

## Team

- Atharva Shah ([@HighnessAtharva](https://github.com/HighnessAtharva)), solo.

## Stack

| Part | Tool |
|---|---|
| Language | Python 3.11 |
| Agent | Claude Agent SDK, model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at medium effort, auth through `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` |
| Tracing | neatlogs Python SDK 1.4.26, neatlogs CLI 0.2.0 |
| Sandbox | Docker Engine 29.8.2 in WSL Ubuntu 22.04, one fresh container per run |
| Docs reader | Firecrawl CLI 1.25.3 |
| Failure classifier | Jev (TypeSafe System One) |
| Session capture | Entire CLI 0.11.4: Checkpoints, Graph, Brain, Trails |
| Business plan | cfo.ai |

## Planning Happened Before the Event

Planning and tool tests happened before the event in a private repo. No FirstRun code was written before kickoff (Sat 2026-10-10, 12:30 PM IST).

## Build Log

### 2026-10-10 (Saturday)

- **12:30 to 13:10 IST.** Created the public repo, ran `entire enable --agent claude-code --search-skill --agent-help-skill` before commit 1, and pushed the Entire config, 6 Trail runners, and the Graph and Brain agent instructions.
- **13:20 IST.** Preflight passed: 4 keys present (lengths only checked), Docker 29.8.2 in WSL, `gh`, Firecrawl 1.25.3, Entire 0.11.4, the venv on Python 3.11. `entire doctor` reports no problems.
- **13:30 IST.** Scaffold: `pyproject.toml`, `src/firstrun/config.py` (the only file that names a model), `src/firstrun/tracing.py`.
  - `python -m neatlogs doctor --probe` passed 8 of 8 checks, including `TRACE_VISIBLE` and `TRACE_FINALIZED`.

# FirstRun ### Docs that work. Literally. FirstRun runs your quickstart in a clean container, finds the first step that breaks, and proves the fix with a second clean run. [![Live site](https://img.shields.io/badge/site-firstrun.atharvashah.com-0A66D6?style=for-the-badge)](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/) [![neatHack 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20for-%23neatHack%202026-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-246%20offline-1B8A3A?style=for-the-badge)](.github) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-3776AB?style=for-the-badge&logo=python&logoColor=white)](pyproject.toml) [**Try it in the browser**](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/) · [**Watch a real run**](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/run.html) · [**See the 4 upstream PRs**](#firstrun-found-4-real-docs-bugs-and-opened-4-upstream-prs) · [**Follow the build on X**](https://x.com/cultist_dev)
The 44-second launch film. The video does not play for you? [Open it on the site](https://firstrun.atharvashah.com/) or [download the MP4](docs/assets/firstrun-launch.mp4).

```bash pip install git+https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun firstrun https://docs.example.com/quickstart ``` ## Break, Fix, Prove Takes 195 Seconds

1. Read
FirstRun reads the page and plans one step per command.
2. Run
Every step runs in a clean container, like a new developer. The first failure stops the run.
3. Prove
A fix is done only when a second clean container passes the whole quickstart.
The input below is a known-broken test fixture (`tests/fixtures/docs/broken_quickstart_FIXTURE.md`), not a real project's docs. Step 3 pins an old chromadb that cannot install on Python 3.11. ```text Step 3 of 4: pip install chromadb==0.3 ERROR: No matching distribution found for numpy~=1.21.6 Cause: docs_bug (source: jev) Patch: step 3 -> pip install chromadb Verified: 4/4 steps passed in a fresh container Time to first success: 195 s ``` FirstRun writes `report.md`, `patch.diff` and `pr_body.md` into the run folder. The patch is one line. ## Six Teams Get a Different Job Out of the Same Engine | # | You are | The problem | Run this | You get | |---|---|---|---|---| | **1** | A DevRel or docs lead | Nobody tests the quickstart after launch day | `firstrun ` | A pass or a verified fix, with a PR draft | | **2** | A release manager | A new release of your package broke the docs and you do not know which one | `firstrun bisect --package ` | The last good and first bad release | | **3** | A technical writer | The docs assume tools the reader does not have | `firstrun prereqs ` | A Prerequisites block, proven in a clean container | | **4** | An open-source contributor | You want a first PR that a maintainer merges | `firstrun pr ` | The `gh` commands for the docs PR, source check included | | **5** | An engineer picking a tool | You want to know if the vendor's quickstart works before you commit | `firstrun ` | A time to first success and the first step that breaks | | **6** | A coding agent | You need a loop that checks its own docs work | `firstrun run --resume ` | State after every step and a model-free verify |
1. Does my quickstart work today? Run it every night.
A DevRel team ships a quickstart once and a dependency moves the week after. The first person to find the break is a new user, and most new users leave instead of filing a bug. ```bash firstrun https://docs.example.com/quickstart ``` A clean pass ends as `passed`. A break ends as `verified` once a second container proves the fix. The nightly check costs about $0.02 per run, measured by neatlogs.
2. Which release broke it, and when? Docs Bisect names the package version.
```bash firstrun bisect --package jafgen ``` FirstRun binary-searches the package's releases, one fresh container per probe, with the version pinned through `PIP_CONSTRAINT`. It replays stored commands, so a bisect makes no model calls. **Real result:** the dbt DuckDB guide never worked in a clean environment. Its step `jafgen --years 6` passes on jafgen 0.3.1 (2023-01-17) and fails on 0.4.6 (2024-04-07). PyPI has no release between them. The guide merged on 2025-03-14, 11 months after `--years` was gone. 5 probes found it.
3. What does it silently assume? Prerequisite Proof writes the missing block.
```bash firstrun prereqs ``` FirstRun turns the container fixes of a run into a Prerequisites block. Then it proves the block. A fresh container with only those items runs the docs as written. | Quickstart | The docs assume | Proof in a clean `python:3.11-slim` | |---|---|---| | AccuKnox knoxctl | curl, ca-certificates, gnupg, sudo | proven, 5/5 steps | | MkDocs | curl | proven, 9/9 steps | | Entire install | curl, git, `~/.local/bin` on `PATH` | proven, 4/4 steps, git found in round 2 | | dbt + DuckDB | Python 3.12 or later, git | steps 1 to 9 pass on `python:3.12-slim`, step 10 is the jafgen docs bug |
4. Open the docs PR. A verified fix becomes an upstream pull request.
```bash firstrun pr ``` FirstRun prints the `gh` commands and a PR body. Every draft gets a source check first, because a docs note can look like a docs bug. FirstRun opened 4 real PRs this way. They are listed [below](#firstrun-found-4-real-docs-bugs-and-opened-4-upstream-prs).
5. Test a vendor before you adopt it. Time to first success is the number.
Point FirstRun at any public quickstart. The report shows how long a new developer needs to reach a working result, and where they get stuck first. No account with the vendor is needed for the steps that run offline.
6. Give your coding agent the loop. Plan, run, recover, verify, with a trace.
The site hands you a prompt for Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. The agent installs FirstRun, checks Docker, runs your quickstart, proves the fix and opens the PR when you say yes. `state.json` is written after every step, so a run resumes with `firstrun run --resume RUN_ID`.
## FirstRun Found 4 Real Docs Bugs and Opened 4 Upstream PRs FirstRun ran five open-source quickstarts whose docs live in public repos. Every finding came from a verified run, where a second clean container passed with the fix.

Create one with `claude setup-token`. - Optional: `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` for traces. - Optional: `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for Jev. Without it, Claude classifies the failure. Install: ```bash pip install git+https://github.com/HighnessAtharva/firstrun ``` FirstRun reads keys from `.env` in the folder you run it from. To use another file, set `FIRSTRUN_ENV_FILE`: ```bash export FIRSTRUN_ENV_FILE=/path/to/your/.env ``` On Windows with Docker in WSL, FirstRun calls `wsl -d Ubuntu-22.04 docker`. On Linux or macOS, set `FIRSTRUN_DOCKER=docker`. Run it on a quickstart URL: ```bash firstrun https://docs.example.com/quickstart ``` A URL tested in the last 24 hours returns the cached result. Add `--fresh` to run it again. Read the result in `runs//report.md`. Build the HTML report with: ```bash firstrun report --html ``` The offline test suite needs no network, Docker or keys: ```bash pytest -q ``` ## One Trace Follows the Docs Page From Read to Verified Fix ```mermaid flowchart TD A[docs URL] --> B["read_docs

[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) lists the states, the failure classes, the budgets and every span. ## Each of the 8 Focus Areas Has a Feature You Can Open | Focus area | Feature | Where you see it | |---|---|---| | Planning | The planner turns the docs page into a runbook | `runbook.json`, the `planner` span | | Tool use | Firecrawl reads, Docker runs, Jev classifies | One TOOL span per call | | State | `state.json` is written after every step | `firstrun run --resume RUN_ID` | | Context | The planner reads only the quickstart page | `read_docs` span input | | Execution | One fresh container per run | `step.N` spans with exit codes | | Recovery | Classify, search, patch, retry up to 3 times | `recover.N` span | | Verification | A model-free re-run in a new container | `verify` span, status `verified` | | Iteration | v1 traces, detections, a fix, v2 traces | The results table below | ## Version 2 Finishes 3 of 4 Quickstarts and Recovers 3 Failed Steps v1 ran with recovery off. v2 ran after the neatlogs planner fix (3ca6f11), with recovery and verification on. The same four targets ran both times. Cost and duration come from the neatlogs traces in [evidence/before_after_traces.json](evidence/before_after_traces.json). Cost is the Sonnet 5.5 list price and is not billed, because the runs use a subscription token. | Target | v1 (recovery off) | v2 (neatlogs fix, recovery, verify) | |---|---|---| | neatlogs Python SDK | passed 3/3 | passed 3/3 | | Entire CLI install | failed at step 1, `curl: command not found` | verified 4/4 after 2 fixes, one of them a real docs fix | | Chroma getting started | passed 3/3 | passed 2/2 | | OpenAI v0 README (fixture, Wayback 2023-08-02) | failed at step 6, `openai: command not found` | pinned `openai==0.28.1`, then stopped honestly: the example needs an OpenAI key | | Metric | v1 | v2 | |---|---|---| | Quickstarts that end passed or verified | 2 of 4 | 3 of 4 | | Failed steps recovered | 0 | 3 | | Fixes proven in a fresh container | 0 | 1 | | Average tool spans per run | 4.25 | 6.0 | | Average cost per run, from neatlogs | $0.0262 | $0.0200 | | Average run time, verification included | 128 s | 201 s | v2 takes longer because a verified fix runs the whole quickstart a second time in a new container. The six mistakes the agent made in v1: 1. The plan changes between runs. The same neatlogs page gave 4 steps, then 3 steps, 5 minutes later. 2. The planner invents steps. It added `command -v entire` and `test -f first_trace.py`, which the docs never say. 3. The planner writes placeholder steps. Chroma step 2 is `true`. 4. A fake secret passes as a step. `export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-...'` exits 0. 5. The planner skips the steps that matter, because they need a key. 6. 9 of 16 steps check only the exit code. ## What Broke While Building - **Git 2.33 hung Entire checkpoints.** The post-commit hook waited 206 s on `git update-ref --stdin`, and the checkpoint was never written. Git 2.55.0 fixed it, and the next hook took 3 s. - **One run split into 3 traces.** The first live run on the neatlogs docs produced 3 traces. The CLI now opens one `firstrun.run` trace around reading, planning, every step and verification. - **Ask-once crashed background runs.** The prompt raised `EOFError` with no terminal. It now returns nothing, and recovery uses the top class. - **Tests exported junk traces.** Each `pytest` run created about 50 empty `neatlogs-app` traces. The test fixture now sets an empty key, and a run after the fix created 0 traces. - **A docs note looked like a docs bug.** On Dagster, FirstRun labeled two gaps as docs bugs. A check of the source showed the page already covers both, in a prerequisite line and a note the planner skipped. FirstRun now opens no PR on Dagster. Every PR draft gets a source check before it ships. - **A cd broke steps three ways.** A leading cd, a cd inside a patched chain, and a file check after cd each failed a step that worked. The container now treats a cd into the folder it is already in as a no-op, and file checks also look from the run root. - **The Entire Brain watcher does not run on Windows.** Brain runs with `--no-daemon` and is refreshed by hand. Known limits are listed in [docs/known-limits.md](docs/known-limits.md). Examples: a hung step is not retried, and version pinning covers pip only. ## Parallel Agents Built It and Entire Reviewed Every Layer - **Build:** a lead session planned the work and ran worker agents in parallel, one track each: fixtures, planner, executor, recovery, verification, report page, then edge cases. All agents ran on Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort. - **Review:** each layer is an Entire Trail, so Entire runners reviewed every commit since kickoff. They found 3 real bugs, all fixed: a secret retry loop, a Windows-only Docker default, and a cd guard that was written but never called. - **CI:** GitHub Actions runs the 246 offline tests on every push and pull request. - **Jury self-test:** the Entire judge plugin, run on this repo with the real start time, ranked it with no excluded work: 3.93 of 5, authenticity 4.5, integrity 5.0.
